question: ____________ is represented by the root apex's constantly dividing cells.
solution:
The correct answer is **__Option- 1__**

**__Explanation - __**

__
 
• The growth of plants occurs only in a particular specific region of the plant. This is because of the dividing tissue, known as Meristematic tissue.
 
• The cells of the meristematic tissue divide actively to form specialized structures such as buds of leaves and flowers, tips of roots and shoots, etc.
 
• These cells help to increase the length and girth of the plant. The meristematic tissues heal the wounds of an injured plant.

**Characteristics of Meristematic Tissue - __**

__
 
• It has the quality of self-renewal as every time the cell divides, one cell remains just like the parent cell and the others form specialized structures.
 
• vacuolesIt has very few small vacuole.
 
• These are living and thin-walled.
 
• The protoplasm of the cell is very dense.
 
• They have single large and prominent nucleus.

 [IMAGE: https://biology4isc.weebly.com/uploads/9/0/8/0/9080078/7462219_orig.jpg] 

**Types of meristematic Tissue -**__ 

Depending on the region **where they are present** , meristematic tissue is classified as -** Apical, Intercalary, and Lateral Meristematic tissue**.

 
 

 **Apical Meristem**
 **Lateral Meristem**
 **Intercalary Meristem**
 
 

 
 __
 
• Present at the tips of the roots and shoots and help in the increase in the height of the plants.
 
 
 
 
 
• Present in the stems and roots on the lateral side.
 
 
 
 
 
• Present within the leaves and internodes at the intercalary position.
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
• Various cell divisions facilitate the growth of the cells in the roots and shoots. and help in cellular enlargement.
 
 
 
 
 
• It increases the thickness of the plant. 
 
• *Vascular cambium and cork cambium* are the 2 lateral meristems.
 
 
 
 
 
• These help to increase the length of the internode. It is in a neighborhood with grass, monocots, and pines.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://www.pmfias.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/03/Meristematic-Tissue-Plant-Tissues.jpg] 

Depending on the** function** Meristematic tissue is of 3 types - **Protoderm, Procambium, and Ground Meristem.**

 
 

 **Protoderm**
 **Procambium**
 **Ground Meristem**
 
 

 
 
 
• It is the outer plant tissue and forms the epidermis.
 
 
 
 
 
• It is the innermost tissue and leads in the rise to the xylem and phloem.
 
 
 
 
 
• The cells are large with thick walls.
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
• It protects the plants from any mechanical shocks.
 
 
 
 
 
• It helps in the transport of water and nutrients to different parts of the plant.
 
 
 
 
 
• It forms the cortex, pericycle, and pith.
